title: Two vLLM Recipes for Blackwell: More Context, More Concurrency, Less VRAM Waste
body:
Blackwell vLLM Recipes: Why NVFP4 KV Matters

I’ve released two vLLM recipes for Blackwell GPUs:

Both are built around the same idea: Blackwell can do native FP4 well, so the KV cache should benefit from it too.

Most people running quantized models are already familiar with FP4/NVFP4 model weights. The model gets smaller, leaving more VRAM for context and concurrency.

NVFP4 KV applies that same idea to the KV cache.

Instead of storing the KV cache in BF16, FP16, or FP8, these builds store it in NVIDIA’s FP4 format.

That matters because KV cache becomes one of the biggest VRAM consumers as context length and sequence count increase.

Smaller KV means more room for:

more concurrent sequences

larger aggregate KV pools

multi-agent and multi-user serving

On a 5090, that can mean the difference between simply supporting 262K context and having enough remaining capacity to serve several useful streams at once.

What makes these different from vanilla vLLM?

These are not just different launch flags.

They combine functionality that is not currently available together in upstream vLLM main as a normal supported Blackwell configuration , including:

MTP or DFlash2 speculative decoding

Blackwell-specific kernel/backend work

high-context concurrent serving

tool-calling and correctness fixes needed for these combinations

A lot of the underlying work comes from existing community PRs, FlashInfer/vLLM development, and other open-source research. I’ve integrated that work, added fixes where needed, and packaged the result into reproducible builds.

The vision tower runs in a CPU sidecar instead of occupying GPU VRAM.

For this type of server, I would rather spend scarce GPU memory on:

weights + KV cache + active sequences

than reserve it for a vision encoder that may only be used occasionally.

You still get multimodal input, while preserving more VRAM for the actual serving workload.

The two builds target slightly different priorities.

~400K usable KV pool in the current 5090 profile

strong decode performance

better fit for multi-agent, multi-user, and long-context workloads

You trade some peak decode speed for more KV capacity.

up to 4 streams in the current capacity profile

substantially faster speculative decode

especially strong single-stream and low-concurrency performance

You give up some KV capacity compared with MTP in exchange for more speed.

These make the most sense if you have FP4-native Blackwell hardware and care about maximizing what one server can do.

That includes setups such as:

2× 16 GB Blackwell cards

other sufficiently large SM120/SM121 systems

They are particularly useful for:

parallel coding/research agents

serving several persistent sessions from one GPU

Who should not use them?

Use normal upstream vLLM if you want the most conservative, officially supported path.

These builds intentionally sit ahead of upstream in several areas. They include community patches and experimental combinations that have not all been merged into vLLM main.

official upstream support

production environments where experimental patches are unacceptable

then vanilla vLLM is probably the better choice.

If you want to push Blackwell harder today, these builds are for that.

The goal isn’t just a giant context number or a faster benchmark.

It’s to make 32 GB of Blackwell VRAM behave like a much more capable serving platform .

Quantized weights reduce model memory.

NVFP4 KV reduces cache memory.

CPU vision avoids wasting VRAM on the vision tower.

The freed memory goes back into context and concurrent sequences.

That’s what makes these builds interesting: more useful work per GPU.

Both recipes have been heavily stress-tested, and they’ve already been cloned and run by other users.

Feedback, PRs, bug reports, benchmark results, and weird workloads are all welcome.

submitted by /u/SeanHighness
summaryZh: 本文分享了针对英伟达 Blackwell 架构 GPU 的两套 vLLM 推理配置方案。该方案核心采用 NVFP4 格式对 KV 缓存进行量化存储，显著降低高上下文与多并发场景下的显存占用。同时集成了 MTP-3 与 DFlash2 投机解码技术，并将视觉编码器移至 CPU 侧运行，从而在 RTX 5090 等显卡上有效节省显存资源，提升长文本吞吐量与并发服务能力。
